astra.quote: W3 unit 38 has a horizontal positive band at row 7, columns 1–10
astra.plain: Unit 38 brightens one full row. It can act as the flat base of a triangle whose bottom sits at row 7.

check.note: All ten values match; in 56 samples unit 38 averages 2.3 when the base is at row 7.

astra.say: The model says another pattern is a bright horizontal line across row 7, nearly the full width of the image.

astra.quote: W1 also emphasizes the upper-middle region
astra.plain: h1 unit 19 reads pixels near the top centre, as if watching for the tip of the triangle. Two large weights are given as evidence.

check.note: Both are the two largest input weights of unit 19, but W1 as a whole is strongest in rows 4 to 8 (row norm 0.61 to 0.77 against 0.17 in row 1).

astra.say: The model says the network also pays special attention to pixels near the top middle of the image.

astra.quote: b3 at the top corners is -0.457 and -0.518
astra.plain: The bias is the output when no hidden unit fires. Strongly negative values at the corners mean those pixels start dark.

check.note: Both values match; (0,0) is -0.4571 and (0,11) is -0.5177.

astra.say: The model says the background stands out from the drawing, with negative starting values at the top corners and nearly zero weights along the top row in most patterns.

astra.quote: The paired diagonals converge near the upper center and spread toward the lower corners.
astra.plain: Extending the two slanted lines, they meet near the top middle and separate going down. That is the outline of a triangle pointing up.

check.note: The lines start at (1,5) and (1,6) and reach (8,1) and (8,10).

astra.say: The model says the two slanted lines come together near the top middle and spread apart toward the bottom corners.

astra.quote: The prominent narrow side patterns favor outlines over solid filled shapes.
astra.plain: The argument is that thin weight lines must mean thin drawn lines. A thin line in W3 can also move the edge of a solid region.

check.note: We ran the model for 56 samples: all were solid, with no gaps inside any row.

astra.say: The model says these thin side lines point to outlines more than solid shapes.

astra.quote: a white outlined, approximately isosceles triangle on black
astra.plain: This is the final answer. Isosceles means the tip sits above the middle of the base.

check.note: In 55 of 56 samples the tip is within 1 pixel of the base centre, but all 56 are solid, so outlined fails.

astra.say: The model says its best reading is a white triangle outline on black, with its two slanted sides about equal in length.

astra.quote: Typically about 8–10 pixels wide and 7–10 pixels tall
astra.plain: This is the size estimate, read from where the longest edges and bars sit.

check.note: In 56 samples widest row is 3 to 9 with 20 at 8 or more; height is 3 to 8 with 19 at 7 or more.

astra.say: The model says a typical triangle is about 8 to 10 pixels wide and 7 to 10 pixels tall.

claude.quote: Every input row for row 0 of the image (pixels 0–11), column 0 and column 11 has weights of about 0.01 or less.
claude.plain: The first layer ignores the outer ring of pixels, so nothing there matters to the network. Shapes never reach the frame.

check.note: 84% of these 34 x 64 weights are at most 0.01; the largest is 0.034, against up to 0.63 elsewhere.

claude.say: The model says the network puts almost no weight on the outer edge of the input image, along the top row and both sides.

claude.quote: So the average image is a wedge: a point at the top centre, widening downward.
claude.plain: The answer treats the output bias b3 as the typical image. A wedge narrowing upward would point to a triangle.

check.note: b3 and the mean of 56 samples are both wedge-like (correlation 0.70), but b3 is not the average: background is about 0.6 higher in b3.

claude.say: The model says the average image is a wedge, pointed at the top middle and getting wider toward the bottom.

claude.plain: Unit 13 of h2 draws the left side of the triangle as a slanted line of positive output weights.

check.note: All seven values match along the diagonal.

claude.say: The model says one pattern is a bright slanted line running from near the top middle down to the left.

claude.quote: Units 20 and 34: positive diagonals from (1,6)/(1,7) down-right to (8,10), e.g. unit 34 has 0.556, 0.461, 0.619, 0.393.
claude.plain: The right side is claimed for two units. Only unit 34 fits, and its inner neighbours are positive too, so it fills beside the edge.

check.note: Unit 34 values match but its line ends at (6,10) and it fires in 2% of samples; unit 20 is a bar on row 10, and unit 21 is the true diagonal.

claude.say: The model says two other patterns are bright slanted lines running from near the top middle down to the right.

claude.quote: Units 21, 49 and 57: positive bars across row 10, e.g. unit 49 has 0.31, 0.45, 0.49, 0.45, 0.36.
claude.plain: Bars across row 10 would give a low flat base. Bars of this kind exist, but in other units than the three named here.

check.note: None of the three has this bar; the quoted numbers are unit 43, row 10, columns 2 to 6. Unit 57 never fired in the samples.

claude.say: The model says three patterns are bright horizontal bars across row 10, near the bottom of the image.

claude.quote: The bottom edge can sit at row 6, 8, 9, 10 or 11.
claude.plain: A base that can sit in several rows means the triangle changes height. The final image then varies from sample to sample.

check.note: In 56 samples the base is in rows 5 to 10, mostly 8 to 10, and never in row 11, whose mean output is -0.96.

claude.say: The model says the bottom of the shape can sit at different heights, on row 6, 8, 9, 10 or 11.

claude.quote: When unit 12 or 11 moves the base, whole rows below the new base go dark.
claude.plain: These units have a bright row with dark rows beneath, so firing one cuts the triangle off higher up. Whole-row darkening only matters if the rows were filled to begin with.

check.note: Unit 12 averages 1.8 when the base is at row 6 or 7, unit 11 averages 1.8 at row 8, and their W3 rows match the pattern.

claude.say: The model says that when certain patterns move the bottom edge up, every row below the new bottom turns dark.

claude.quote: All of these fit a solid triangle. A thin outline would only change the base row and the two side pixels.
claude.plain: If the shape were an outline, a change of base would touch only a few pixels. Whole dark rows mean a filled region is being cut.

check.note: We ran the model for 56 samples: all were solid triangles with no gaps inside any row.

claude.say: The model says all this fits a solid triangle, because an outline would need only the bottom row and two side pixels changed.

claude.quote: A single solid white triangle on a black background, pointing up. The tip is near the top centre (row 1–2, columns 4–7).
claude.plain: This is the final answer, and it is the only one of the three to say filled. The tip position is given as a narrow range.

check.note: 56 samples are solid upward triangles, but only 16 have the tip in rows 1 to 2; the tip ranges over rows 1 to 7.

claude.say: The model says each image is one solid white triangle pointing up on black, with its tip near the top middle.
